title: Refusal
description: The body of a refusal the control plane answers a request of the provisioner contract with, application/json, as the integration contract's refusal, https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/refusal.schema.json. The codes the adapter that serves a node pool meets: 401 unauthorized, unsigned and the same whatever the cause, as that refusal lists them, a request whose signature the control plane has already seen among them, under the replay rule of https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json; 403 forbidden, a request outside the access key's rights, a claim of a pool the adapter does not serve, and a request naming a dispatch_id that is unknown or that belongs to another adapter, all the same answer as an unknown pool, so nobody learns whether an id exists; 400 unsupported_contract_version, an X-Qory-Contract-Version the control plane does not serve; 400 invalid_request, a body that breaks its schema; 413, a request over 1 MiB; 409 no_gateway, a claim whose run's pool choice resolves to no gateway; 409 handed_over, a second handover of a dispatch; 409 not_dispatched, a handover before dispatched; 409 lease_expired, a dispatched or a handover after the lease lapsed, when the dispatch has gone back to the queue; 410 gone, a request of a dispatch that ended because its work item was closed or undone; 429 rate_limited, with Retry-After, the seconds the adapter waits before it sends the request again, built anew, as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes a retry. No refusal is tied to a step or to a policy. A 401 is unsigned; every answer to a verified request is signed. A member this schema does not define is refused.
